newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt policies helping exporters, says Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt policies helping exporters, says Peters.

text.p: The New Zealand government's economic policies were giving the export sector the stability and certainty it needed to make investment decisions, Treasurer Winson Peters said on Thursday.

The value of the New Zealand dollar had been stable since the beginning of the year, interest and inflation rates were falling and the government fiscal position was very strong, he said in response to a critical Australian and New Zealand union report on the state of New Zealand manufacturing.
Even at the bottom of the current economic slowdown, growth remained above 2 percent, higher than experienced in the 1970s and 1980s, Peters said.
"If the critics of government policies are seeking some sort of pump-priming exercise, they had better realise that would be thoroughly bad for the export sector in the long-term," he said.
Peters said the government was working on reducing compliance costs faced by businesses and those benefits would flow to the country's wealth creators.

Peters said that in the first four months of this year, the value of manufactured exports had risen 30 percent ot NZ$409 million, while the value of metal exports had risen nearly 25 percent to $129 million.
